list: Official 55 trophies, as published on PlayStation Network (via Exophase and PSNProfiles, November 2026). Names, descriptions and grades are PlayStation's own words; every guide below is written for this companion, in its own words, and names its source.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum lands the moment the other 54 trophies are all yours, so there is no separate task here — the whole companion is the guide to it. Expect a long haul: PowerPyx puts the platinum at about 200 hours and Push Square at 250 hours or more, most of it the 100% completion checklist rather than the story. One playthrough is enough, there are no online trophies, and nothing here needs a second character run. The one hard rule for the whole run: cheats switch trophies off on this save, and they also stop the game saving, so keep them off the file you take to the platinum.
trophies.source: PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide; Push Square GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players will earn and it cannot be missed — just play the story from the start and it pops when the mission ends. It is one of the 12 hidden story trophies, which stay hidden on PlayStation until you earn them, so expect it to appear without warning in your list.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles (as listed by Planet GTA 6)

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and this unlocks with the chapter's close. The story runs five chapters and takes about 60 to 80 hours by PowerPyx's estimate, so Chapter 1 is only the warm-up. PowerPyx notes the chapter trophies can pop a little late, after the first mission or two of the next chapter, so do not worry if it does not fire the instant the credits roll on the chapter.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 2 to its end. Chapter 2 is where the two leads start roaming together, which matters for the partner trophies further down this list, so it is worth doing the optional missions that appear along the way — 100% completion later needs any 100 of them, and the ones you do now count. Like the other chapter trophies, this one may pop a mission or two into Chapter 3 rather than at the chapter's final cutscene.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. By this point several side strands have opened — Andy's calls Lucia, Tyrone's labs work is Jason's, Randy's car wish list is live — and playing them as they appear keeps the later cleanup short. The chapter trophy itself is automatic: complete the chapter's missions and it unlocks, possibly a mission or two into Chapter 4.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4, the longest stretch of the story. Bank jobs open through an optional mission in this chapter, and those vaults feed two trophies of their own, so take the bank-job thread when it appears rather than leaving it for after the story. The trophy is unmissable and fires as the chapter closes, give or take a mission into Chapter 5.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold for finishing the story: complete the final mission in Chapter 5 and this unlocks with it. It is the only gold tied to the story itself — the other gold is A Long Road, for 100% completion. There is no mission replay in this game, so the final mission plays once; free roam continues afterwards, and everything left on the list can still be earned.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is one of the six named main missions with its own trophy, and it unlocks automatically when you finish that mission in the story. You cannot miss it and you cannot do it early — it arrives when the story brings it, so just keep playing the main missions in order.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a named story mission with its own trophy, so finish the mission and the trophy follows. It is one of six such mission trophies spread across the story — one in Chapter 2, one in Chapter 3, three in Chapter 4, one in Chapter 5 — and all six are automatic and unmissable.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named story mission, and completing it earns this trophy on the spot. Like the other five mission trophies it is story-locked and unmissable: there is no way to finish the game without it, and no way to fail it permanently, since missions can be retried from a checkpoint.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission with its own trophy. Play the main missions in order and it unlocks when the mission ends. There is nothing to prepare and nothing to miss — the mission arrives in the story's flow, and the trophy is one of the 12 hidden story trophies that stay concealed on PlayStation until earned.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a named story mission set around Vice City International Airport, and finishing it earns the trophy. It is automatic and unmissable. Note the airport itself matters for another trophy — Catch Me If You Can, for stealing a passenger jet from a gate — so once the story has taken you to VCIA, you will know your way around it for the open-world attempt later.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a named story mission, and this trophy unlocks when you complete it. It is the last of the six mission trophies and, like the rest, it is automatic: play the story missions in order and it will come to you. No preparation, no alternate route, and no way to miss it.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold, and the real platinum gate: reach 100% on the completion checklist, which appears after the story under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion. Work you did during the story already counts. PowerPyx calls the checklist lenient — closer to 60% true completion — but it is still the biggest single job: 70 of the 80 challenges, 15 of the 18 meditation spots, 300 stunts, all 8 bank vaults, all 39 gang operations, and everything in the shooting ranges, drone races and Bret's hunting decks. Push Square's version of the same list is stricter, asking for 15 of the 18 card sets too. Do the story first, then work the checklist in the roadmap's second stage, and this gold follows the cleanup.
trophies.source: PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide; Push Square GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off any 250 stunts and this silver pops — stunt jumps, flights under bridges, knife flights and base jumps all count, and PowerPyx counts 397 stunts in the world, so there is slack. Keep in mind the 100% checklist wants 300, so the habit to build is doing a stunt whenever you pass one, not grinding all 250 in one sitting. Every stunt you land during the story already counts toward both numbers.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. PowerPyx lists them as fishing, hunting, golf, shooting ranges, pool, basketball, a video game, a race and a stunt. You do not need to win or finish any of them — one attempt at each is enough — so the fastest route is a tour of Leonida: fish once, hunt once, play a round of golf, fire a round at a range, shoot a game of pool, play basketball, finish a video game, enter a race and land a stunt. Most of these feed other trophies, so this one tends to pop while you are working on them.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in every one of the 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is a skill trophy rather than a grind: each challenge has its own gold threshold, so expect to replay the harder ones and to spend time learning the range layouts and the weapons they favour. The ranges also count toward the 9 activity types for Master of None, and the checklist needs the ranges finished too, so gold here is doing double duty for the platinum.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Each location is its own race, so work through them one by one and tick them off in the tracker as you go — the counter on PlayStation tracks how many locations you have won at. Drone races are a distinct activity from car and bike races, so the wins here do not count toward Earn Cash, Not Kudos, and the checklist wants the drone races finished as well.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The key word is different: winning the same race twenty times does not count, so enter new events across Leonida and keep a note of which ones you have already won — the tracker here is built for exactly that. Races count toward the activity types for Master of None, and the fastest car you own is usually worth more than the fastest line, so upgrade before you chase the last few wins.
trophies.source: PlayStation trophy list, via Exophase and PSNProfiles (as listed by Planet GTA 6)

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. You meet Cal in Chapter 1, and after that he texts you a fishing spot — follow the text, go to the spot, and take the challenge. Fishing is also one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so the first cast does double work. If you lose the challenge, you can try again; the trophy is about beating him once, not about a single attempt.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Play any one in-game video game through to the end. PowerPyx notes three of them run on the TV at home and a fourth sits on arcade machines, so the easiest route is the living room: sit down, pick a game, and finish it. A video game also counts as one of the 9 activity types for Master of None, so this trophy and that one can pop on the same evening.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's side strand. This one is Lucia only, and it starts with a phone call in Chapter 3 — answer it and follow the strand through to its final mission. Side strands are not part of the main story, so if you rush the chapters you can walk straight past the call; check your phone for missed contacts after each chapter and start any strand that has opened before moving on.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's treasure diving strand, which runs to 7 shipwrecks in total. Kenton goes quiet after Chapter 1 and returns later in the story, so do not panic if he disappears — he comes back, and the strand can be finished after the story. Dive each wreck he marks, work through to his final mission, and the trophy pops. Nothing here is missable.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand at the mud club in Kelly County. It opens in Chapter 2, so head out to the mud club once you can roam and start the strand there. Like the other stranger strands it stays open after the story, so there is no deadline — but starting it when it opens keeps the post-story cleanup short.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. Not every side questline counts — PowerPyx notes it is still confirming exactly which strands qualify — so the safe approach is to finish more than eight: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and Bret all have strands with their own trophies, and there are further stranger strands beyond them. Everything here can be done after the story, so treat this silver as a post-story sweep: work the map, answer every call, and let the count build.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's strand, which is a wish list of 16 sports cars to find and deliver. It opens in Chapter 3. The cars are the work: spot them around Leonida, steal or buy as the strand asks, and hand them over one by one until the list is done and the final mission unlocks. Scanning new vehicles with the WAiNK app as you go also feeds Whip It Good, so keep the phone out while you hunt.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand by shutting down the labs in Vice City. This one is Jason only, and it runs from Chapter 3. Work through the lab locations Tyrone marks, clear each one, and the strand ends with its final mission. Like the other stranger strands it stays available after the story, so there is no missable risk — just a set of locations to clear.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. This is the one trophy PowerPyx flags as possibly missable, and the reason is a single morning in Chapter 1: at Jason's house, Lucia says she is going to meditate and walks out to the balcony. Follow her and accept the optional quest — she shows you how meditation works. That morning is gone after Chapter 1, and while the trophy officially needs the 18 marked spots, PowerPyx reports the balcony session raised the meditation counter by one even though it is not marked as a spot, so nobody has confirmed whether it is required. The protection costs one minute: do it when it comes up. Push Square lists no known missables, so this is a caution, not a certainty — but it is the only caution on the whole list. The other 18 spots are all visitable after the story, and 100% completion needs 15 of them.
trophies.source: PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide; Push Square GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. This strand is Jason only and opens from Chapter 2. PowerPyx has not confirmed which animal triggers it, so the reliable route is the thorough one: clear all 15 of Bret's target decks, which the 100% checklist needs anyway, and the unique hunt should be covered along the way. Hunting also counts toward the activity types for Master of None, and studying animals through the binoculars feeds the checklist's 100-of-255 target without having to hunt them all.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets out of 18 in total. Cards are scattered across Leonida, so this is a collecting trophy that rewards steady pickup rather than a single hunt: grab every card you pass during the story, and use the map to sweep the ones you missed afterwards. Push Square's version of the 100% checklist asks for 15 of the 18 sets, so the three sets for this silver are only the start — keep collecting and the checklist will thank you.
trophies.source: PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide; Push Square GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK phone app at 100 locations. Landmarks, curiosities and sculptures all count, so the habit is simple: whenever you arrive somewhere new, open WAiNK and scan it. Scanning vehicles with the same app feeds Whip It Good, so the phone does double work on every outing. The count is cumulative across the whole game, and nothing about it is time-limited.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the 80 challenges. Challenges are the small goals layered across everything you do — driving, shooting, exploring, earning — so this bronze arrives naturally while you chase the rest of the list. Keep an eye on the challenge screen and pick off the easy ones when you want a quick win, but remember the 100% checklist needs 70 of the 80, so the last twenty are still waiting after this one pops.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then escape the heat. This is possible once both characters can roam together, from Chapter 2 onward. The practical route is to build the wanted level deliberately — bank jobs hand out 4 stars anyway — and then break line of sight, hide, and wait for the stars to clear with your partner still alongside. If the stars drop while you are alone, it does not count; bring your partner and try again.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner, without losing your wanted level between them. Plan the route first: pick three shops close together, rob each in turn, and keep moving — the wanted level has to survive the whole run. PowerPyx notes the trophy pops about 30 seconds after the third shop, so do not stop and wonder if it worked; keep driving and it will fire. If you lose the heat mid-run, the chain breaks and you start the three again.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Scanning them with the WAiNK app is enough — you do not have to drive them — so the habit is to scan every new vehicle you pass. The 100% checklist raises the bar to 200 of the 277 base-model vehicles, so keep scanning long after this bronze pops; the same habit that earns this one is the habit that finishes the checklist.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. The detail that matters is who counts: PowerPyx reports gang members count, while soldiers, police and civilians seem not to. So pick a fight with a gang — a group of them, close together — trigger Combat Focus, and drop five before it ends. If you try it on police, the count will not move; find a gang instead and try again.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Steal a passenger jet docked at a gate at Vice City International Airport and fly about 1 km away from it. You will know the airport from the story mission VCIA Takedown; come back in free roam, get to a gated jet, get it moving and get it airborne. Expect heavy police attention on the ground, so plan the approach — a fast vehicle to the gate, then straight into the jet — and do not stop to fight on the tarmac.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Steal a military tank. PowerPyx found the tanks at Mile Zero Air Station in the southwest of the map, so that is the place to aim for. Getting in and getting out with a tank draws the heaviest response in the game, so go in with a plan for the escape — the trophy is about taking the tank, and the escape is what makes it stick.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. You need the Snap Gun for this one, which a Chapter 3 main mission gives you, so it cannot be done before then. With the tool in hand, case the store, wait for the quiet moment, and get in and out without tripping a detection — if you are spotted, leave and try again rather than fighting through it, since detection is what fails the attempt.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Bank jobs open through an optional mission in Chapter 4, and there are 8 vaults in total — the 100% checklist needs all 8, so this silver is the halfway mark, not the end. Each vault is its own job with its own escape, so take them one at a time and tick them off as you go; the escape counts, so a vault robbed without a clean getaway does not move the number.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. The first bank job counts for this one, so it may pop on its own during the Chapter 4 bank thread. If you want it earlier, PowerPyx notes you can blow open a truck's back door with a sticky bomb and take the cash that way — either route works, as long as you get away clean afterwards.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — all 52 areas on the PlayStation tracker. The practical way to clear the fog from the whole map is from the air: a plane covers ground far faster than any car, and a systematic sweep of the state will clear the last pockets. Combine the flight with WAiNK scanning and you will feed the vehicle and location counts at the same time.
trophies.source: PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list (count)

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Every gang has its own operations, so the work is finding one per gang and hitting it — the tracker is useful here, since the count is per gang, not per robbery. The 100% checklist raises the same task to all 39 operations, so keep robbing after this bronze pops; the routes and hideouts you learn now are the ones the checklist will ask for again.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. The exact method has not been confirmed by the guide writers yet — the description tells you where, not how — so the sensible approach is to head to Ocean Beach, find a bar or vendor with a view of the water, and order a cocktail there. This is one of the hidden side trophies whose method is still being worked out, so if it does not pop on the first try, try a different spot along the beach. It is not missable; the beach is always there.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The method is not yet confirmed by the guide writers, but the description is the hint: get a vehicle inside a showroom, then drive it straight out through the glass. Pick a showroom with a big front window, build speed inside if you can, and aim for the glass. It is a hidden side trophy and it is not missable — showrooms do not close.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. The trigger is a gang operation, not a game of bowling: take all 3 key valuables from the Kingpin Bowling gang operation in Port Gellhorn. PowerPyx notes the robbery comes back later if you miss it, so it is not missable — if the operation is not there when you first visit, come back and it will be. Bowling itself is one of the activities, but the trophy is about the valuables, not the score.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Max out strength on both Jason and Lucia. Work out together and both make progress, so the efficient route is joint sessions at the gym rather than grinding one character and then the other. One honest note on this trophy: Push Square does not mark it hidden, while the other trackers count it among the 28 hidden trophies — either way, the task is the same, and it is not missable.
trophies.source: PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide; Push Square GTA 6 trophy guide

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Do 500 things that change your criminal profile. PlayStation tracks a count to 500, and the count climbs from the ordinary business of being a criminal in Leonida — jobs, robberies, getaways, and the choices the game offers along the way. It comes naturally over a full playthrough, so do not grind it early; play the story, work the open world, and check the counter now and then. If it is short at the end, the remaining points are whatever profile-raising acts you have left on the map.
trophies.source: PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list (count)

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm. The method is not yet confirmed, and PowerPyx suspects a link to a Payday Loans store — the name and the description both point at failing once and succeeding on the second try. If the Payday Loans lead holds, the shape of it is to attempt something there, fail, and succeed on the retry. Treat this one as unconfirmed for now: it is a hidden side trophy, it is not missable, and the guide writers are still pinning down the trigger.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? The method is not yet confirmed, and PowerPyx suspects a UFO questline — the description reads like a reaction to something strange in the sky or in the world. If the UFO lead holds, the route is to follow the strange sightings rather than the main story. This is a hidden side trophy with an unconfirmed method, so check back as the guide writers pin it down; nothing about it is missable, and the world stays open after the story.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl them over with a melee drive-by. The in-game hint points to a melee attack from a moving vehicle, and PowerPyx suspects a kick from a motorcycle — the shape of it is to ride past someone on a bike and land the kick. Try it on a lone target on a quiet road rather than in a crowd, so you can see whether the attempt registered, and repeat until it pops. It is a hidden side trophy and it is not missable.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 in marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robberies, and the total adds up across all of them — this is a running total, not a single haul. The dye pack jammer, which makes laundering smoother, unlocks in a Chapter 3 main mission, so the rate improves once the story has taken you there. Keep laundering after every job rather than letting bills pile up, and the quarter-million arrives on its own.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Guns, car mods and tattoos get you there fastest, and the total is cumulative across every shop in the game, so ordinary spending during the story already counts. If you are short at the end, the quickest top-up is the expensive end of the gun store and the mod shop — buy what you will actually use, since the money is gone either way.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 purchasable garages. PowerPyx puts the total at $160,000, and the real estate app that sells them arrives in Chapter 2. Garages are not just a trophy — they are the storage that On the Spot needs, since the Scooter Bros app registers vehicles you own and keep. Buy them as you can afford them through the story, and finish the set once the money is there.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. You need garage space first, so pair this with Little Boxes — buy the garages, store the vehicles, then register them in the app. Any ten vehicles count, so register the ones you already own rather than hunting for rare ones, and the trophy pops on the tenth registration.
